back: A cell whose structure is adapted to carry out a particular function.
A group of cells with similar structures working together to perform a shared function.
A structure made of a group of tissues working together to perform specific functions.
A group of organs with related functions working together.
Cilia on their surface beat to sweep mucus (with trapped dust and bacteria) up the airways, away from the lungs.
A long, thin root hair gives a large surface area for absorbing water and mineral ions.
They contain many chloroplasts to absorb light for photosynthesis, and are packed near the upper surface of the leaf.
Haemoglobin carries oxygen; no nucleus leaves room for more haemoglobin; biconcave shape gives a large surface area; flexible for capillaries.
Flagellum for swimming; many mitochondria for energy; acrosome enzymes to digest a way into the egg.
Large energy stores in the cytoplasm; a jelly coat that changes after fertilisation so only one sperm enters.
Very long fibres carry electrical impulses over long distances; branched endings connect with many other cells.
